title: Ferdinand of Aragon, king of Sicily, to his father John II: cipher passages of 5 June 1473 (Hostalric) and 3 Nov 1474 (Zaragoza) (BNE MSS/20211/64 and /73)

steps.what: Galende Díaz 1994 lists /56 (1470) and /73 (1474) as ciphered letters of Ferdinand to John II, with no key; /64 not listed; no edition found.
d64: nine cipher lines (201 signs) and the interlinear notes transcribed from the 1085-px scan at 4-6x.
d64 key from the interlinear words and letters (dela gente, de castilla, de aragon, traygo, semana, hi seran): first decode builds sentences (troops for Perpignan).
d64 doubtful signs re-read at 8-16x: b. r, Q f, a. i, -o- i, ooo ll, 3- y, qo o; place sign FI noted barçna (Barcelona); 'irán' for 'havrán'.
d64 p-sign split by shape (hooked = o, plain = c): the plain p also gives o (ochocientos, ciento).
d56 (1470) transcribed: 15 lines, about 330 signs, a different (probably syllabic) cipher with a faint pencil decipherment; not attacked.
d73: eleven cipher lines (310 signs) transcribed; interlinear letters read on line strips at about 7x, about half legible.

d73 19-sign key from the legible interlinear letters decodes 'no res menos se', 'matrimoni... in / fanta mi hermana no se', 'mossen s...'; the clear paragraph at the foot of the page begins with the same words.

align1474.py aligns the 310 signs with the paragraph's 325 letters and re-estimates the key (2 passes); about 30 signs valued; 'si aya' and 'a bueltas' settled from the cipher; 'rompido' kept after a 12x check.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 310 tokens, 47 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -3.311 per letter; polyphonic: 20% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Prior-art review after the reading: DECODE R1183 and R1177 opened (Decrypted, no document listed); Tomokiyo, 'Spanish Ciphers before Accession of King Ferdinand: 1470-1479' (Academia.edu, Nov 2018) found, abstract and blog read, paper not read because it is a paid download. The 29 Oct record of no prior reading corrected. No key compared.

MSS/20211/61 (Alcalá, 13 Mar 1473), not in the earlier lists, carries cipher runs in lines 7-18 of the recto (18 runs, 279 signs, blind shape transcription) with contemporary interlinear notes. The 1473 key (dec1473.py, unchanged) was applied under a protocol written beforehand: 0.68 of the note letters recovered (semi-global edit distance, 166 letters, 232 signs under notes) against at most 0.40 for 200 shuffled keys (mean 0.31); 11 of 36 note words found exactly (shuffled at most 5). Same cipher as /64; below the 0.85 bar set for a validation, and the glossed portion is under 300 signs, so not a validation of the key. Files: transcription/d61_transcription.md, decryption/d61_decode.txt, check61/.

Validation test of the 1473 key on MSS/20211/61, bar set beforehand by the contributor (0.85 of the note letters and 0.30 over the best shuffled key; by the contributor's record): 0.68, and 0.28 over the best of 200 shuffled keys (0.40). Failed: the key of /64 is not validated by /61.

Integration check of PR #619: check61/score61.py re-run (0.6807 of 166 note letters, 11 of 36 words, shuffled keys at most 0.3976, mean 0.307: result.json reproduces); 1,000 further shuffles at most 0.404; an independent decoder gives the same 18 decodes. The sibling identification of /61 stands; the validation test is recorded as failed in the step before. Order of events by the contributor's record. BNE Digital answered 403, so the runs were not sampled against the image.

validation.notes: polyphonic: 20% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: d64: key rebuilt from the contemporary interlinear notes and extended by sense. d73: key read from the interlinear letters, then aligned on the clear paragraph on the same page, which is the plaintext.
outcome.fraction_read_source: d64: 199 of 201 signs read (two open, 13 places with a value chosen by sense); d73: all of the passage read from the clear paragraph, with three doubtful words.

credits.note: Directed Claude Code in transcribing BNE MSS/20211/64 and /73, rebuilding both keys and reading both cipher passages (catalogue #857); /56 transcribed.
Interlinear notes on /64 and /73 and the clear paragraph on /73 (BNE MSS/20211).

Found that BNE MSS/20211/61 (Alcalá, 13 Mar 1473) is in the 1473 cipher of /64 and tested Michael Brackx's key, unchanged, on its glossed runs (PR #619, 14 Nov 2026): 0.68 against a bar of 0.85, so a sibling identification, not a validation of the key.

gaps.detail: the 1085-px scan does not separate the forms

texts.label: Hostalric, 5 June 1473 (MSS/20211/64)
texts.summary: Ferdinand reports the troops he brings for the relief of Perpignan: his continos and the men from Castile, more than 500 horse from Aragon, the Valencians (some already at Barcelona), 800 horse in all with 100 men-at-arms.

reading_review.note: Read the reading file as sentences in Spanish and checked it against the English translation; coherent, with the holes the NOTES list. Not checked against the page image by a person.

texts.label: Zaragoza, 3 Nov 1474 (MSS/20211/73)
texts.summary: Ferdinand is astonished that the infanta Juana's marriage has not been broken off as negotiated, and asks that Mossèn Santcliment be the one sent to Naples, so that his own affairs are handled with the others.

reading_review.note: Read the reading file as sentences in Spanish and checked it against the English translation; coherent, with the holes the NOTES list. Not checked against the page image by a person.

outcome.notes: Contributed; reading_review to be recorded by the reviewer. Prior reading unsettled (2 Nov 2026): see conditions.prior_solution. first_break left unset until Tomokiyo 2018 is read.

prior.where: DECODE R1183 (/64) and R1177 (/73), status Decrypted since 26 Aug 2019, no document listed on the record view and Inline Plaintext: Yes, so the status may reflect only the interlinear notes. Tomokiyo, 'Spanish Ciphers before Accession of King Ferdinand: 1470-1479' (Academia.edu, Nov 2018): reconstructs ciphers of Ferdinand's 1470s letters to John II; not read (paid download), so whether it treats /64 and /73 is unconfirmed. Galende Díaz 1994 lists /56 and /73 with no key. Contemporary interlinear notes on /64 and /73 and the clear paragraph on /73.

human: Outside contribution: Michael Brackx chose the target, set the rounds (transcribe, key from the notes, re-read doubtful signs at higher zoom, siblings, review) and approved each step. Transcription, keys, decodes and readings were done by Claude Code under his direction.
